trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
trophies.guide: The platinum. It pops automatically the moment the other 54 trophies are all earned, so there is nothing extra to do beyond finishing everything else on this list. Work through the roadmap in order — story first while the missable flags are still reachable, then strangers, activities, collectibles and money — and keep rotating manual saves so a single missed moment never costs you a restart. When only this and A Long Road remain, check the in-game completion stats for the last stragglers.

Before you push into Chapter 2, this is a good moment to grab In The Beginning… on Ocean Beach, which this guide flags as an early-game moment (see its entry), and to make a manual save you can reload.

trophies.name: A Long Road
trophies.guide: Reach 100% on the game's own completion checklist. In this series that means the story, every stranger strand, the collectible sets, the activities and the exploration targets all count together, so use the in-game stats screen as your source of truth and work region by region. This guide's roadmap stages mirror that split: story, strangers, activities and crime, collectibles and exploration, then money and property. The trophy pops the moment the counter hits 100%.

trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
trophies.guide: Complete 250 stunts. Stunts are the game's marked jumps and aerial tricks; the in-game stats keep a running count, and this tracker mirrors it with a counter you can tick up as you go. Work them in a fast car or on a bike, and clear them area by area as the map opens — 250 is a grind if left to the end, but painless spread across the story. A stunt only counts when the game registers a clean landing, so retry any that end in a crash.

trophies.name: Master of None
trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of activity at least once. Open the map legend and visit one of each activity icon — races, drone races, fishing, bowling, arcade, shooting range and the rest — and start each one. You do not need to win, only to try. Tick them off against the activity icons as you go; the trophy unlocks when the last untried type is started.

trophies.name: The Shootist
trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn gold in every Shooting Range challenge — PlayStation tracks 42 of them. Each challenge scores accuracy and speed, so learn the target patterns, use the weapon class each challenge specifies, and upgrade your weapons before the harder tiers. Gold usually needs a near-perfect run: if you miss the medal, restart immediately rather than finishing a doomed attempt. The counter in this tracker follows the 42-challenge total.

trophies.name: Top Fun
trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race once at each location that hosts one. Find the drone race icons on the map, win at every distinct spot, and keep a note of which locations are done — the requirement is per location, not per race, so repeat wins at the same spot do not advance it. Fly the course once slowly to learn the gates, then push for the win.

trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — different is the key word: winning the same race 20 times does not count. Use the race menu to pick events you have not won yet, across road, off-road and water classes, and track wins with the counter here. A tuned vehicle in each class makes this much easier; if a race keeps beating you, come back with a faster ride rather than grinding attempts.

trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge. Find Cal at a fishing spot and take his challenge; you need to out-fish him under the challenge rules (heaviest catch or most fish, as the challenge states). Fish the same water he does, watch where the big fish bite, and do not rush your casts. If he wins, challenge him again straight away — the trophy only needs one win.

Five strands have their own trophies (Andy, Kenton, Billy, Randy and Tyrone), so finishing those puts you at 5 of 8; find three more strangers by exploring — their markers appear as question marks or character icons when you are near. A strand only counts when its final mission is done, so always run a strand to its end. Use the counter here to track strands as they close.

trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret. This guide flags it as missable: the description ties it to one named character's request, and character requests in this series can close when their strand ends. When Bret asks for the hunt, do it before finishing his other business, and keep a save from before his strand's final mission. Track the animal where Bret sends you, hunt it cleanly, and deliver as instructed. Flag basis: the official description names a single character and a unique target; treat it as one-time until proven otherwise.

trophies.name: Hot Together
trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: With your partner alongside, raise a 4-star Wanted Level, then lose it and fully escape the heat. Build the stars together (a robbery spree with your partner present works — see Retail Therapy), then break police line of sight: swap vehicles out of view, use tunnels, garages or the countryside, and stay hidden until the stars clear completely. The trophy needs the escape, not just the chase, so do not re-engage once you are nearly clear.

trophies.name: Retail Therapy
trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob 3 shops in a row with your partner while your Wanted Level stays up the whole time. Plan a tight route of three nearby shops, keep a fast car running outside, and move fast between tills so the stars never drop to zero. If the heat fades between shops, stir it back up before entering the next one. Afterwards, losing that same heat cleanly can also set up Hot Together if you reached 4 stars.

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down 5 enemies during one activation of Combat Focus. Set it up where enemies cluster — a gang hideout, a robbery gone loud, or a mission firefight — then trigger Combat Focus with at least five targets in reach and drop them before the effect ends. A high-capacity weapon helps; if you only get four, reload the save and try a denser spot rather than hoping for a bigger crowd.

trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA, the airport. This guide flags it as missable: the story mission VCIA Takedown (Hi-Jacked) is the obvious window, when the airport is in play. During or around that mission, get to a plane and take off without permission — an unscheduled departure — then escape the resulting heat. Save before the VCIA missions so you can retry. Flag basis: the official description ties the act to one named place that the story visits for a specific mission; earn it while that window is open.

trophies.name: Challenging Tank
trophies.guide: Get into a Rhino tank. The description is a joke about the heat inside one, and the act it points at is stealing or driving a Rhino — found at military sites such as a base or airfield. Expect a heavy Wanted Level the moment you take it; the trophy is about getting in and driving, so grab it, roll out, and survive as long as you can. Save before the attempt so a failed grab costs nothing.

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store without being detected. Go at night, approach quietly, and keep every witness and camera from raising the alarm: move crouched, avoid the staff's line of sight, and grab the take without a shot fired or a Wanted Level gained. If you are spotted, leave and reset rather than forcing it — detection is exactly what this trophy forbids. Save outside the store so retries are instant.

trophies.guide: A partnership milestone: the description points at doing things together with your partner until your partnership reaches a personal best. In practice that means partner activities — races, outings and jobs done as a pair, including the partner trophies Hot Together and Retail Therapy. Keep choosing partner activities when they are offered and watch the partnership progress in the menus; the trophy unlocks when the partnership hits its mark. This is the vaguest description on the list, so treat partner time as the requirement and check the in-game stats for a partnership meter.

trophies.name: Actions Speak Louder
trophies.guide: Make the story choices the game puts in front of you — the description says it plainly: choices made, for better or worse. This guide flags it as missable because choices are one-time: when a mission asks you to pick a side, a target or an outcome, that moment does not come back on the same save. Save before any mission that smells like a decision point, make the choice deliberately, and keep the pre-choice save until the trophy pops. Flag basis: the official description is entirely about choices, which by nature cannot be replayed without reloading.

trophies.name: Bad Luck, I Guess
trophies.guide: Second time's the charm: fail something once, then succeed on the retry. This guide flags it as missable because a first-try success can skip the setup entirely — if you never fail, there is no second time. When a mission, race or challenge goes wrong, do not reload an old save to erase the failure; use the game's retry and succeed on the second attempt. If you have been reloading every failure, deliberately fail a short challenge once, then complete it. Flag basis: the official description describes a fail-then-succeed sequence that perfect play can bypass.
